note: Scenario catalog of the attribution engine evaluation. Declared BEFORE the first run and not edited after seeing results: the report records the SHA-256 of this file. Synthetic data from our own simulator (src/adapters/health-sim): the numbers verify the engine's logic under these assumptions, not clinical validity.

magnitudeSd.note: Per injected anomaly, uniform. Unit: the person's own day-to-day SD of that indicator (process plus measurement), known to the simulator. Small effects (2-3 SD) are expected to be hard to detect.

durationDays.note: Number of consecutive mission days the effect lasts, uniform integer.

onsetOffsetDays.note: First affected day = firstDay + warmupDays + offset, uniform integer. Offset 0 is the first judged day, so the warm-up has at least 28 normal days and the episode ends at least 4 days before the end of the run.

cabinExcursionTiming.note: The excursion starts at 22:00 the evening before the first affected day and ends at 07:30 of the last affected day, so every morning reading of the episode sits inside it and past the documented lags (heart rate and temperature 6 h, sleep 12 h).

scenarioTypes.name: No anomaly
scenarioTypes.description: Normal mission days only. False-alarm control.

scenarioTypes.name: Individual fever
scenarioTypes.description: One crew member's body temperature rises; the cabin stays nominal.

scenarioTypes.name: Individual heart rate
scenarioTypes.description: One crew member's resting heart rate rises; the cabin stays nominal.

scenarioTypes.name: Cabin heat, whole crew
scenarioTypes.description: Cabin temperature goes above 27 C overnight; resting heart rate and body temperature rise in all 3 crew, the two indicators that have a documented link to cabin temperature in cabin.json.

scenarioTypes.name: CO2 above limit, two crew
scenarioTypes.description: Cabin CO2 goes above its NASA limit; sleep drops in 2 of the 3 crew. CO2 is only linked to sleep in cabin.json, so only sleep is affected.

scenarioTypes.name: Shared, not environmental
scenarioTypes.description: All 3 crew sleep less (for example a schedule shift) while the cabin is nominal.

scenarioTypes.name: Confounder: heat plus unrelated glucose
scenarioTypes.description: Cabin temperature goes above 27 C while one crew member has an unrelated rise in fasting glucose, an indicator with no documented link to any cabin variable. The cabin must not be blamed.
